question: to the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy Irene Montero (The Left), Isabel Serra Sánchez (The Left) Subject:

On 19 May 2026, the US Department of the Treasury imposed sanctions on, among others, the European citizens Saif Abukeshek and Jaldía Abubakra for their participation in the civil society initiative Global Sumud Flotilla and for their links to the Samidoun organisation, respectively. The purpose of these sanctions is to freeze their assets and financial interests located in the United States or under the control of US individuals and companies – including financial transactions – thereby leaving them in a state of vulnerability and defencelessness. These sanctions have been imposed without prior judicial process and are based on ideological assumptions that have not been proven in accordance with due legal guarantees, demonstrating that this is a politically motivated persecution and a violation of their fundamental rights. 1.

Does the Vice-President/High Representative consider that the imposition of sanctions by the United States against European citizens for their participation in initiatives promoting solidarity with Palestine may infringe their fundamental rights, in particular the freedom of expression, association and political participation?
How does the Vice-President/High Representative intend to ensure that the increasing use of sanctions regimes is not employed as an instrument of political repression?

How does the Vice-President/High Representative intend to safeguard the political liberties and fundamental rights of these citizens, who are being persecuted by a foreign country, namely the United States?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (31.7.2026) 1. The EU respects the intention and the right of those on board of the Global Sumud Flotilla ships to draw attention to the humanitarian plight of the population of Gaza. Freedom of expression and freedom of peaceful assembly and association are human rights enshrined in international law, in the European Convention on Human Rights, and in the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. The EU is firmly committed to protect and support civic space and an enabling environment for civil society everywhere. 2. The EU opposes any legislation, regulation or practices that unduly limit freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association, and urges States to repeal or amend measures that penalise individuals or civil society organisations for exercising those rights. In this respect, attacks against participants of the Global Sumud Flotilla or reprisals against them constitute a breach of international law, including international human rights law and international humanitarian law. The delivery of humanitarian aid, food, medicine, or other emergency supplies should be exempted from sanctions, as provided in the UN Security Council Resolution 2664 (2022) and transposed by the EU across its sanctions regimes. The EU considers that sanctions, whether adopted by the UN Security Council or autonomously by the EU, must be grounded in international law, targeted, proportionate and accompanied by appropriate procedural safeguards, including respect for the rights of listed persons. 3. The EU supports independent investigations into all alleged violations of international law. The EU uses various tools at its disposal to stand up for human rights around the world, including through bilateral contacts with the United States and other countries.
